Louis Couperus, The Tour, translated by Alexander Teixeira de Mattos.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/louis-couperus/the-tour/alexander-teixeira-de-mattos

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Louis Couperus, the author, died 1923.
- Alexander Teixeira de Mattos, the translator, died 1921.

First publication of the text used: 1920 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from Dutch in 1920 by Alexander Teixeira de Mattos.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1920, before 1931; a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2015.
- Country of origin (the facts do not name the country of first publication; the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa, and the Netherlands, the country of the original Dutch text): each of these countries has a term of life + 70 years or less. The last person to die did so in 1923, so the text is public domain in each of them from 1 January 1994 at the latest.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
